en.title: Plans and intentions
en.summary: Be going to expresses a plan or an intention.

paragraphs: Be going to + base form expresses a plan or an intention decided before the moment of speaking. It is also used for predictions based on what you can see or know now.

items: We **are going to move** next month.
Look at those clouds! It **is going to rain**.

blocks.html:
FormExample
statementI am going to leave. / She is going to leave.
questionAre you going to leave?
negativeThey are not (aren't) going to leave.
short formI'm, you're, she's going to

paragraphs: Use going to for plans made before you speak, and for predictions with evidence. Use will for decisions made at the moment of speaking, and for general predictions.

blocks.html:
Going toWill
I'm going to buy a car. (I have decided)I'll buy this one. (deciding now)
It's going to rain. (I see clouds)It will probably rain. (my opinion)
We're going to have a party. (a plan)Shall we have a party? I'll cook.

paragraphs: You can also use the present continuous for fixed arrangements (I am meeting her at six) and the verbs plan, intend and hope for intentions: I plan to travel in the summer.

items: Wrong: **I'm going to to the shop.** Right: **I'm going to the shop.** (movement) or **I'm going to buy bread.** (plan)
Wrong: **She going to leave.** Right: **She is going to leave.**
Wrong: **It will rain, look at the clouds.** Better: **It's going to rain, look at the clouds.**
